Daily Devotional

December 13

19 Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble. 20 But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead? (James 2:19-20 KJV)

This is quiet a sarcastic statement, but is so true. The devils, and Satan himself, know that there is only one God, but they certainly are not saved. Knowing about God and Jesus does not get you saved, and if that is all you have is the knowledge of them then you are no better off than the devils are. It takes more then knowing about them to be saved. The bible teaches that you will know the tree by the fruit it produces. If you have no fruit (actions) in your life, because of your salvation, then you likely were not truly saved. There will be many people in hell that thought they were saved, but were not truly born again (Matthew 7:22-23). You can not be truly saved, and yet have no actions showing that you were born again. A born again believer in Jesus will always have a desire to live for God and not the devil. You will try to live holy, as He is holy (1 Peter 1:15), but we all still fail occasionally.

What James is saying is that faith by itself is not enough to get you saved, as even though you are saved by faith (Ephesians 2:8), if it does not cause you to do works of faith, then it is not true faith, and will not save you. If you have true godly faith in Jesus, it will cause you to do works of faith, and this is different than the works of the law. If you have saving faith you will want to serve God out of love, not to get anything from God, but only to respond to the love He has shown us. Anyone who says they have saving faith in Jesus, and yet do nothing to show that they have been born again, and have no fruit (actions) to show from their salvation, they are not truly saved, as saving faith will always produce actions of faith. If you make Jesus your Lord (Romans 10:9-10), and take up your cross to follow Him (Matthew 16:24), you will do the works of faith just because you love Him so much. Therefore faith without works is truly dead. If you are doing things (actions) to try to please God, or earn something from Him, it is works of law. If you do the same things, but just because of His love for you, it is works of faith. Your motive for doing things is what matters to God. Praise God for His plan of salvation!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
